The compilation errors "invalid storage class for function" and "expected declaration or statement at end of input" are typically caused by incorrect macro definitions, specifically when multi-line macros are not properly terminated with a backslash (`\`) on each line. This leads the preprocessor to prematurely end the macro definition, causing subsequent code to be parsed incorrectly (e.g., as a standalone compound statement at file scope, or as code inside an unintended scope).

In `tests/lib/heap_kasan/src/main.c`, the macros `ASAN_COMMON_TESTS`, `ASAN_STR_TESTS`, `ASAN_EXT_TESTS`, and `ASAN_GRANULE1_TESTS` are defined as sequences of `ZTEST_F` calls. Each `ZTEST_F` call is followed by a `{ ... }` block containing the test logic. For these macros to expand correctly, every line within their definition (except the very last one if it's a single token) must end with a backslash.

The current definitions are missing the trailing backslash on their last `ZTEST_F` line, causing the `{ ... }` block of the last test in each macro to be parsed outside the macro definition. This results in a syntax error at file scope, leading to the reported compilation failures.

The fix involves adding a backslash to the last `ZTEST_F` line within the definition of each of these four macros.
